formats.parameter-file: A parameter file of the working group's schemas, in YAML.

sources.name: ProbOnto
sources.citation: Swat MJ, Grenon P, Wimalaratne S (2016). ProbOnto: ontology and knowledge base of probability distributions. Bioinformatics 32(17):2719-2721. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btw170

rows.name: standard-normal
rows.label: standard normal
rows.definition: The measure on ℝ with density φ(z) = exp(−z²/2)/√(2π) with respect to Lebesgue measure.

rows.name: pushforward
rows.label: pushforward

arguments.name: map
arguments.meaning: a measurable map f from the measure's set

rows.definition: f∗μ(B) = μ(f⁻¹(B)), the law of f(X) when X has law μ.

rows.name: conditioning
rows.label: conditioning on a set

arguments.name: set
arguments.meaning: a measurable set A with μ(A) > 0

rows.definition: μ|A(B) = μ(B ∩ A)/μ(A), the law of X given X ∈ A. Truncation is conditioning on an interval.

rows.name: kernel-product
rows.label: product with a kernel

arguments.name: kernel
arguments.meaning: a Markov kernel κ from the measure's set to a set Y

rows.definition: (μ ⊗ κ)(A × B) = ∫_A κ(x, B) μ(dx), a measure on the product of the two sets: draw X from μ, then Y from κ(X, ·).

rows.name: affine-pushforward
rows.label: affine map
rows.definition: The pushforward under z ↦ a + b·z.

rows.name: exponential-pushforward
rows.label: exponential map
rows.definition: The pushforward under z ↦ exp(z).

rows.name: support
rows.label: support
rows.definition: The smallest closed set of full measure, recorded by its infimum and supremum, whether the infimum is attained, and the mass at the infimum.

rows.name: mean
rows.label: mean
rows.definition: E[X], where it is finite.

rows.name: moments
rows.label: moments
rows.definition: E[X^k]: the orders k for which it is finite, and its closed form in the canonical coordinates where it has one.

rows.name: log-moments
rows.label: moments of the logarithm
rows.definition: E[(ln X)^k], for a law on (0, ∞), with the orders k for which it is finite.

rows.name: atoms
rows.label: atoms
rows.definition: The points of positive mass and their masses.

rows.name: mean-one
rows.label: mean one
rows.definition: E[X] = 1. A constraint defines a subfamily; the reduced parameterization it induces is that subfamily's chart.

rows.name: normal
rows.label: normal
rows.definition: The law of μ + σZ, Z standard normal.

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the mean

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation

rows.name: mean-variance
rows.label: mean and variance

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the mean

coordinates.name: v
coordinates.meaning: the variance

rows.provenance: ProbOnto 2.5, Normal2, with its conversion to Normal1.

rows.name: lognormal
rows.label: lognormal
rows.definition: The law of exp(μ + σZ), Z standard normal.
rows.measure: LogNormal(μ, σ) = exp∗ aff(μ, σ)∗ N(0, 1)

rows.name: meanlog-sdlog
rows.label: mean and standard deviation of the logarithm

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the mean of ln X

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation of ln X

rows.name: mean-one-lognormal
rows.label: lognormal with mean one
rows.definition: The lognormal laws whose mean is one.

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation of ln X

rows.name: point-mass
rows.label: point mass
rows.definition: All mass at one point. A family of its own: the normal with zero variance and the lognormal with zero spread are two of its charts, not members of those families.

coordinates.name: x
coordinates.meaning: the point

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the point

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the logarithm of the point

rows.name: point-mass-at-one
rows.label: point mass at one
rows.definition: The one law all of whose mass is at one; the parameter files' only way to switch a shock off.

rows.name: interval-conditioning
rows.label: truncation to an interval

arguments.name: lower
arguments.meaning: the lower bound l; -inf for none

arguments.name: upper
arguments.meaning: the upper bound u; inf for none

rows.definition: Conditioning on the interval [l, u], which must have positive measure.

rows.name: truncated-normal
rows.label: truncated normal
rows.definition: The law of μ + σZ given l ≤ μ + σZ ≤ u, Z standard normal.
rows.measure: TruncatedNormal(μ, σ, l, u) = (aff(μ, σ)∗ N(0, 1))|[l, u]

rows.name: mean-sd-bounds
rows.label: the normal's mean and standard deviation, and the bounds

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the mean of the normal before truncation

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation of the normal before truncation

coordinates.name: l
coordinates.meaning: the lower bound; -inf for none

coordinates.name: u
coordinates.meaning: the upper bound; inf for none

cross_references.note: TruncatedNormal1 (mean, stdev, lowerBound, upperBound), whose bounds are finite

rows.name: truncated-lognormal
rows.label: truncated lognormal
rows.definition: The law of exp(μ + σZ) given l ≤ exp(μ + σZ) ≤ u, Z standard normal: the exponential of a normal truncated to [ln l, ln u].
rows.measure: TruncatedLogNormal(μ, σ, l, u) = (exp∗ aff(μ, σ)∗ N(0, 1))|[l, u] = exp∗ ((aff(μ, σ)∗ N(0, 1))|[ln l, ln u])

rows.name: meanlog-sdlog-bounds
rows.label: the mean and standard deviation of the logarithm before truncation, and the bounds

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the mean of ln X before truncation

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation of ln X before truncation

coordinates.name: l
coordinates.meaning: the lower bound, in the draw's units; 0 for none

coordinates.name: u
coordinates.meaning: the upper bound, in the draw's units; inf for none

rows.name: mean-one-truncated-lognormal
rows.label: truncated lognormal with mean one
rows.definition: The truncated lognormal laws whose mean is one. Their chart is the parameter files' TruncatedLogNormal: the standard deviation of the logarithm after truncation, and the bounds in standard deviations of the normal before truncation.

rows.name: sd-log-standardized-bounds
rows.label: the standard deviation of the logarithm after truncation, and the bounds in standard deviations

coordinates.name: sd_log
coordinates.meaning: the standard deviation of ln X, after truncation

coordinates.name: bot
coordinates.meaning: the lower bound, in standard deviations of the normal before truncation; -inf for none

coordinates.name: top
coordinates.meaning: the upper bound, in standard deviations of the normal before truncation; inf for none

rows.name: unit-uniform
rows.label: uniform on the unit interval
rows.definition: Lebesgue measure on [0, 1].

rows.name: uniform
rows.label: uniform
rows.definition: The law with constant density on [a, b].
rows.measure: Uniform(a, b) = aff(a, b − a)∗ U(0, 1)

coordinates.name: a
coordinates.meaning: the lower endpoint

coordinates.name: b
coordinates.meaning: the upper endpoint

rows.name: mean-one-uniform
rows.label: uniform with mean one
rows.definition: The uniform laws centered at one. Their chart is the parameter files' Uniform, whose half-width below one keeps every value positive.

coordinates.name: w
coordinates.meaning: the half-width

rows.name: standard-gumbel
rows.label: standard Gumbel
rows.definition: The measure on ℝ with distribution function exp(−exp(−z)), and so density exp(−z − exp(−z)).

rows.name: type-1-extreme-value
rows.label: type I extreme value (Gumbel)
rows.definition: The law of μ + sG, G standard Gumbel, with distribution function exp(−exp(−(x − μ)/s)): the taste shock of logit choice.

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: the location, which is the mode

coordinates.name: s
coordinates.meaning: the scale

rows.name: finite-mixture
rows.label: finite mixture
rows.definition: Σⱼ wⱼ μⱼ: draw a label j with probability wⱼ, then a value from μⱼ. It is the product of the categorical law on the labels with the kernel sending j to μⱼ, projected onto the value.

rows.name: finite-discrete
rows.label: finite discrete law on real points
rows.definition: The law putting mass pᵢ at each of finitely many real points vᵢ, at least two.
rows.measure: Σᵢ pᵢ δ(vᵢ), a finite mixture of point masses

coordinates.name: values
coordinates.meaning: the points, strictly increasing

coordinates.name: probs
coordinates.meaning: their probabilities

rows.name: mean-one-finite-discrete
rows.label: finite discrete law with mean one
rows.definition: The finite discrete laws on positive points whose mean is one. Their chart is the parameter files' Discrete: the points are the model, not a quadrature of another law.

coordinates.name: values
coordinates.meaning: the points, positive and strictly increasing

coordinates.name: probs
coordinates.meaning: their probabilities

rows.name: categorical
rows.label: categorical
rows.stated_set: the positions 1, …, n of a finite set of labels
rows.definition: The law drawing the label in position i of a finite set with probability fᵢ. Bellman-SYM also takes its weights as the rows of a matrix, or as the one row a previous state selects; the latter is the categorical law at that row.

rows.name: weights
rows.label: the weights, in the order of the labels

coordinates.name: f
coordinates.meaning: the probability of each label

rows.name: bernoulli
rows.label: the probability of the second of two labels

coordinates.name: p
coordinates.meaning: the probability of the second label

cross_references.note: Bernoulli1 (probability), on {0, 1} rather than on two labels

rows.name: finite-markov-kernel
rows.label: finite Markov kernel
rows.definition: A Markov kernel on finitely many real points: from the point in position i, the next draw is xⱼ with probability Πᵢⱼ. Bellman-SYM writes it with either of two names; given a third argument, the previous state, a declaration is the kernel at that state.

state.name: i
state.meaning: the position of the current point

rows.name: transitions-points
rows.label: the transition matrix and the points

coordinates.name: Pi
coordinates.meaning: the transition probabilities, row i the law from point i

coordinates.name: points
coordinates.meaning: the points, strictly increasing

rows.name: lognormal-mixture
rows.label: lognormal mixture
rows.definition: A finite mixture of lognormal laws, at least two. Its components are compared as a set: the same components in another order, or a component split in two, write the same law.
rows.measure: Σⱼ wⱼ LogNormal(μⱼ, σⱼ), the mixture over the components of exp∗ aff(μⱼ, σⱼ)∗ N(0, 1)

rows.name: components
rows.label: the weights, and each component's mean and standard deviation of the logarithm

coordinates.name: weights
coordinates.meaning: the components' weights

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: each component's mean of ln X

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: each component's standard deviation of ln X

rows.name: mean-one-lognormal-mixture
rows.label: lognormal mixture with mean one
rows.definition: The lognormal mixtures whose mean is one. Their chart is the parameter files' LogNormalMixture: ln X = c + Y, Y drawn from component j with probability wⱼ, each component's mean of Y stated relative to the others, and one common shift c making the mean one.

rows.name: relative-means
rows.label: the weights, each component's relative mean and standard deviation of the logarithm

coordinates.name: weights
coordinates.meaning: the components' weights

coordinates.name: mean_log
coordinates.meaning: each component's mean of ln X less the common shift

coordinates.name: sd_log
coordinates.meaning: each component's standard deviation of ln X

bellman-sym.spelling: Mixture((w₁, LogNormal(c + m₁, s₁)), …), with c making the mean one
bellman-sym.head: Mixture

rows.name: truncated-lognormal-mixture
rows.label: truncated lognormal mixture
rows.definition: A finite mixture of truncated lognormal laws, at least two. Its components are compared as a set; a component truncated on neither side is a lognormal.
rows.measure: Σⱼ wⱼ TruncatedLogNormal(μⱼ, σⱼ, lⱼ, uⱼ)

rows.name: components
rows.label: the weights, and each component's canonical truncated-lognormal coordinates

coordinates.name: weights
coordinates.meaning: the components' weights

coordinates.name: mu
coordinates.meaning: each component's mean of ln X before truncation

coordinates.name: sigma
coordinates.meaning: each component's standard deviation of ln X before truncation

coordinates.name: l
coordinates.meaning: each component's lower bound, in the draw's units

coordinates.name: u
coordinates.meaning: each component's upper bound, in the draw's units

rows.name: mean-one-truncated-lognormal-mixture
rows.label: truncated lognormal mixture with mean one
rows.definition: The truncated lognormal mixtures whose mean is one. Their chart is the parameter files' TruncatedLogNormalMixture: ln X = c + Y, Y drawn from component j with probability wⱼ, component j a normal truncated at bounds in standard deviations of that normal before truncation, stated by its mean, relative to the others, and its standard deviation, both after truncation, with one common shift c making the mean one.

rows.name: relative-means-standardized-bounds
rows.label: the weights, each component's relative mean and standard deviation of the logarithm after truncation, and its bounds

coordinates.name: weights
coordinates.meaning: the components' weights

coordinates.name: mean_log
coordinates.meaning: each component's mean of ln X after truncation, less the common shift

coordinates.name: sd_log
coordinates.meaning: each component's standard deviation of ln X after truncation

coordinates.name: bot
coordinates.meaning: each component's lower bound, in standard deviations of its normal before truncation; -inf for none

coordinates.name: top
coordinates.meaning: each component's upper bound, in standard deviations of its normal before truncation; inf for none

parameter-file.spelling: {TruncatedLogNormalMixture: {components: [{weight: w₁, mean_log: m₁, sd_log: s₁, bot: b₁, top: t₁}, …]}}
parameter-file.head: TruncatedLogNormalMixture

bellman-sym.spelling: Mixture((w₁, TruncatedLogNormal(μ₁, σ₁, l₁, u₁)), …), computed from the chart
bellman-sym.head: Mixture

rows.name: piecewise-linear-pushforward
rows.label: piecewise-linear map
rows.definition: The pushforward under the nondecreasing piecewise-linear function through the knots; an abscissa listed twice is a jump.

rows.name: quantile-table
rows.label: quantile table
rows.definition: The law whose quantile function Q, the inverse of the distribution function, is linear between the points of a table: Q∗ U(0, 1). A stretch where u and Q both rise has a flat density; one where u rises and Q stays flat is a point mass; a u listed twice, with Q higher the second time, is a gap in the support. The normal form removes an interior point that lies on the line through its neighbors, which adds nothing; the canonical chart admits none.
rows.measure: Q∗ U(0, 1), Q piecewise linear through the points (uᵢ, qᵢ)

rows.name: points
rows.label: the points of the table

coordinates.name: u
coordinates.meaning: the probabilities, from 0 to 1

coordinates.name: q
coordinates.meaning: the quantiles there

domain_conditions: first(u) == 0 and last(u) == 1 and first(diff(u)) > 0 and last(diff(u)) > 0

rows.name: mean-one-quantile-table
rows.label: quantile table with mean one
rows.definition: The quantile tables on positive values whose mean is one. Their chart is the parameter files' Tabulated, whose checker accepts a mean within 10⁻¹² of one; the table is the law, not an approximation of one.

rows.name: points
rows.label: the points of the table

coordinates.name: u
coordinates.meaning: the probabilities, from 0 to 1

coordinates.name: q
coordinates.meaning: the quantiles there, positive

domain_conditions: first(u) == 0 and last(u) == 1 and first(diff(u)) > 0 and last(diff(u)) > 0
